question: Which Rajput ruler founded the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty in Malwa during the 8th century CE?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagabhatta I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nagabhatta I** was the founder of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty in Malwa during the 8th century CE.
 
• The Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty was known for resisting Arab invasions, particularly in the western regions of India.
 
• Nagabhatta I expanded his kingdom and established his capital at **Ujjain**, a significant cultural and political center.
 
• He laid the foundation for the dynasty's dominance in northern India, which reached its peak under rulers like Mihira Bhoja.
 
• The Gurjara-Pratiharas played a vital role in preserving the Indian subcontinent from external invasions and ensured the continuation of Indian culture during their rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gurjara-Pratihara Dynasty:** This dynasty is considered one of the prominent Rajput dynasties that ruled northern India between the 8th and 11th centuries.
 
• **Military Achievements:** The Pratiharas were instrumental in defending India against Arab invasions, particularly from the west.
 
• **Socio-Cultural Contributions:** They were patrons of art, architecture, and literature, contributing significantly to the development of Indian culture during their reign.
 
• **Mihira Bhoja:** A notable ruler from the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty under whom the empire reached its zenith, particularly excelling in military and administrative capabilities.
 
• **Decline of the Dynasty:** The dynasty eventually weakened due to internal conflicts and external invasions, paving the way for the rise of other regional powers like the Chandelas and the Palas.
